Its collaborators include the contemplative-AI researcher Ruben Laukkonen and the neuroscientist Morten Kringelbach, a link to int/a-adjacent science.

Works on Agency, Multi-agent · Key work Four faces of information (Nature Reviews Physics) (2026); A unified taxonomy of information dynamics (PNAS) (2025); AI in a vat (Reinforcement Learning Journal) (2025) · Get involved No openings advertised; the contact is the director (f.rosas@sussex.ac.uk)

Note Launch date and grant sizes were not found. Independent coverage is limited to Iliad's listing of incubated organisations. The publication list includes members' work from before the lab (2018-2024). The director remains a lecturer at the University of Sussex, and the contact address is a Sussex one.

Bridge ring 14

Active Inference Institute Bridge

Nonprofit · Distributed · founded 2022 · also draws on Formal, Psychology

A volunteer-led US 501(c)(3), run online, for research and education on Karl Friston's active inference and free energy principle. It has 2,000+ community members and 700+ livestreams, runs textbook study groups, research fellowships, software projects (e.g. Generalized Notation Notation) and the annual Applied Active Inference Symposium (6th edition 12–13 Nov 2026, online and free). Since June 2025 it has hosted a $270k Survival and Flourishing Fund grant for the AI Capabilities & Alignment Consensus Project, led by Adam Safron.

Active inference gives a formal, neuroscience-derived account of agency, world models and preferences. The institute is one of the few places where that community works directly on alignment: an SFF-funded project on the meaning of 'world models' and 'agency' that aims to bridge 'doomers' and 'accelerationists', plus fellowship projects on alignment coalitions and on subjectivity in artificial agents.

Works on Agency, Epistemics · Key work AI Capabilities & Alignment Consensus Project (AICACP): journal collections, workshops and media; SFF grant of $270k (2025); Research fellowship project 'AI²C: Active Inference Alignment Coalition' (Mahault Albarracin) (2026); 6th Applied Active Inference Symposium (12–13 Nov 2026) (2026) · Get involved 6th Applied Active Inference Symposium, 12–13 Nov 2026 (online, free; presenters and sponsors sought); Weekly textbook study groups (e.g. Namjoshi, 'Fundamentals of Active Inference'); Volunteer, internship, research-fellowship and mentorship programmes

Note Volunteer-run, so output quality varies. It is closely networked with VERSES AI (Friston is its chief scientist, and Albarracin works there), which markets 'intrinsically safe' active-inference agents without strong public evidence; claims that active inference solves alignment are unproven. It became an institute in 2022, growing out of the earlier Active Inference Lab. The roster's ring 'potential' was raised to bridge because of the SFF-funded alignment project.

Amaranth Foundation: NeuroAI for AI Safety Bridge

Funder · New York, USA

The Amaranth Foundation is a longevity and neuroscience philanthropy that says it has committed over $50M since 2021 to work on brain ageing, centenarian genetics, neurotechnology and NeuroAI. Its NeuroAI team, led by Patrick Mineault, produced 'NeuroAI for AI Safety' (arXiv, Nov 2024; revised Apr 2025) with 15 authors from the foundation, Basis, Convergent Research, E11 Bio, Stanford's Enigma Project, the Allen Institute, Yale and NYU. The roadmap assesses routes from neuroscience to safer AI: brain-like sensory representations, embodied digital twins, biophysical models, cognitive architectures, fine-tuning on brain data, loss functions taken from biology, and neuroscience methods for interpretability.

It is the main reference document for using neuroscience as a source of AI-safety methods, a route the ML-centred field has largely ignored. A funder from outside the AI-safety ecosystem that has staff on this question is rare.

Works on Agency, Assurance, Values · Key work NeuroAI for AI Safety (roadmap, arXiv 2411.18526) (2024); NeuroAI for AI safety: A Differential Path (LessWrong post) (2024); 'Does the solution to building safe artificial intelligence lie in the brain?' (The Transmitter) (2025) · Get involved Newsletter and contact address (neuroaisafety@amaranth.foundation) on neuroaisafety.com; No open grant call for NeuroAI safety found for 2025-26

Note No visible grant programme or institutional follow-through on the roadmap in 2025-26 beyond talks and essays. Founders and legal seat are not given on its site: the NeuroAI lead is based in New York, while grant databases list a Philadelphia address. Brain-inspired AI could also speed up capabilities, a tension the roadmap itself raises with its 'differential' framing.

Astera Institute (Neuro-AI: Obelisk AGI programme, Astera Neuro, and Steve Byrnes's brain-like-AGI safety) BridgeOn aisafety.com

Nonprofit · Emeryville, United States · founded 2020 · also draws on AI minds

A philanthropic research institute in Emeryville, California, founded and funded by Jed McCaleb. Its Neuro-AI division runs Obelisk, a brain-inspired AGI programme led since February 2026 by Dileep George, and Astera Neuro, a neuroscience programme on how brains produce conscious experience, led by Chief Scientist Doris Tsao. Astera also employs Steve Byrnes, who writes on brain-like-AGI safety, hosts the interpretability group Simplex (profiled separately), and runs a life-sciences division (Radial) and a residency programme.

It is the largest private bet on deriving AI from neuroscience. One institution holds both the claim that brain-like AI will be easier to understand and control (McCaleb) and the warning that brain-like RL agents are a dangerous route to AGI (Byrnes). Byrnes's attempt to reverse-engineer human social instincts as an alignment target is a distinctive neuroscience-based approach to what AI should value.

Works on Agency, Values · Key work Neuroscience programme launch with Doris Tsao ($600M+ over a decade) (2025); Dileep George joins Astera to lead its neuro-inspired AGI effort (2026); Intro to Brain-Like-AGI Safety (new version, Steve Byrnes) (2026) · Get involved Careers page with Neuro and AGI research roles (astera.org/careers); Astera Residency Program, run by the Foundation division; Postbac and internship programmes planned by Astera Neuro

Note Obelisk is a capabilities effort: its aim is to build AGI, and the aisafety.com map files 'Astera Neuro-AI' under capabilities research. Its safety case rests on the unproven claim that brain-like systems will be more interpretable and controllable, while its own safety researcher, Byrnes, argues brain-like RL is a dangerous path. The roster entry merged Simplex, which is profiled separately to avoid double-counting.

Brain-inspired Cognitive Intelligence Lab (BrainCog Lab), Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences Bridge

Academic · Beijing, China · founded 2013 · also draws on Philosophy

A lab at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Automation in Beijing, founded in June 2013 and directed by Yi Zeng. It builds brain-inspired AI on spiking neural networks: the BrainCog engine and the BORN engine for what it calls 'living' AGI. A recurring line of its work argues that AI safety and morality should come from brain-like self-models, theory of mind and empathy rather than external constraints. Papers include a 2022 theory-of-mind network for reducing risks to other agents, altruistic and moral agents built on brain-inspired empathy (2024-25), and 'Super Co-alignment' (2025). Zeng also founded the institute's International Research Center for AI Ethics and Governance and is founding dean of the Beijing Institute of AI Safety and Governance.

It is the clearest non-Western bridge from neuroscience to alignment. It treats alignment as something grown from within, through empathy and self-modelling, rather than imposed, which gives a contrasting alignment target. Zeng links this lab work to Chinese and UN AI governance.

Works on Values, Agency · Key work A Brain-Inspired Theory of Mind Spiking Neural Network for Reducing Safety Risks of Other Agents (Frontiers in Neuroscience) (2022); BrainCog: a spiking-neural-network-based brain-inspired cognitive intelligence engine (2022); Building Altruistic and Moral AI Agent with Brain-inspired Emotional Empathy Mechanisms (2025) · Get involved BrainCog is described as an open platform for brain-inspired AI and brain simulation (braincog.ai); no open calls, jobs or events found in 2025-26

Note The lab also pursues 'living AGI' and 'conscious living AI', so its safety work sits beside a capabilities agenda. The lab website's news section has not been updated since 2022, so activity was confirmed through papers. Beijing-AISI, which Zeng founded and leads as dean, is on the classic map, but this lab is not.

Civilization Research Institute (CRI) / The Consilience Project Bridge

Nonprofit · Asheville, USA · also draws on Philosophy, Safety science

A US 501(c)(3) research centre in Asheville, North Carolina, focused on catastrophic and existential risk and on criteria for a global civilisation 'wise enough to steward' exponential technology without catastrophe or dystopia. Its published research includes 'Reality Check' (January 2025), 'Steps for Prudent Problem-Solving', and a 'General Regulatory Process for Advanced Technology' that treats AI as an exponential technology with exponential risks needing proof of safety and global coordination. Its publication, The Consilience Project (Daniel Schmachtenberger, Zak Stein and others), published essays on sensemaking, information warfare and technology, but no longer publishes regularly; its latest article dates from July 2024.

It is the main institutional source of the metacrisis vocabulary int/a uses for AI race dynamics: multipolar traps, Moloch, the 'third attractor'. It places AI risk inside a wider analysis of how civilisation's problem-solving generates catastrophic risk. Its regulatory framework draws on precedents from aviation and toxic products rather than ML-specific policy.

Works on Metacrisis, Epistemics, Assurance · Key work Reality Check (2025); General Regulatory Process for Advanced Technology; Technology is Not Values Neutral: Ending the Reign of Nihilistic Design (The Consilience Project) (2022) · Get involved Staff roles in Asheville and remote (chief of staff, research analyst, engineering, finance), listed on its careers page and Idealist; Contact form for people offering skills or resources

Note Public output is sparse and mostly undated: The Consilience Project says it is 'no longer releasing new articles at a regular cadence', and the regulatory framework carries no date. The CRI website names no leadership; its Idealist listing (joined August 2026) names Daniel Schmachtenberger as executive director. The taxonomy uses this entry as a dormant example, but the January 2025 report and 2026 hiring meet the 'active' rule. The founding year is not stated; the website dates from at least 2020.

Club of Rome Bridge

Nonprofit · Winterthur, Switzerland · founded 1968 · also draws on Peace

A membership organisation of scientists, economists, business leaders and former officials, founded in 1968 in Rome and based in Winterthur, Switzerland, since 2008. It is known for the 1972 report The Limits to Growth, and it now works through Material and Cultural Transformations pillars that include Earth4All and a Systems Transformation Hub for EU policy. On 16 March 2026 it issued an open letter, signed by more than thirty leaders including co-president Paul Shrivastava and Millennium Project director Jerome C. Glenn, that calls AGI an existential risk and asks the UN to hold a special General Assembly session solely on AGI governance.

It is the best-known systems-and-limits institution to adopt loss-of-control language about AGI, and it has UN and EU access. It can place AI risk within polycrisis and planetary-boundaries framings for audiences that AI-safety groups do not reach.

Works on Metacrisis, Security · Key work Open letter calling for a UN General Assembly special session on AGI (2026); The Limits to Growth (1972); Earth for All: A Survival Guide for Humanity (Earth4All) (2022)

The January 2026 AI policy covers its own use of AI, not AI governance. The ring follows the taxonomy's worked example (bridge); on the evidence alone it sits near potential. Wikipedia's list of co-presidents is out of date (it still names Sandrine Dixson-Declève); the site's governance page names Shrivastava and Zimmermann del Castillo.

Concordia (Google DeepMind) Bridge

Programme · London, UK · founded 2023 · also draws on Arts, futures

An open-source Python library (Apache 2.0) from Google DeepMind for generative agent-based modelling. Agents driven by large language models act in natural language in simulated physical, social or digital settings, while a 'game master' entity, borrowed from tabletop role-playing games, decides what happens. First released in 2023 and rebuilt as version 2.0 in July 2025 (v2.4.0 came out in March 2026), it is used for social-science simulation and for testing how LLM agents cooperate. One such use was the Cooperative AI Foundation's Concordia Contest at NeurIPS 2024.

It lets social scientists study norms, cooperation and conflict among AI agents without building ML infrastructure. It also gives cooperative-AI researchers a shared testbed for evaluating agents in mixed-motive situations. The team's 'theory of appropriateness' brings sociology and cognitive science into how AI behaviour should be judged.

Works on Multi-agent, Assurance · Key work Generative agent-based modeling with actions grounded in physical, social, or digital space using Concordia (2023); A theory of appropriateness with applications to generative artificial intelligence (2024); Concordia library v2.0 (2025) · Get involved Open source: install gdm-concordia from PyPI and contribute through GitHub issues and pull requests

Note This is a software project inside a frontier lab, not an organisation, and Google DeepMind sets its priorities. Simulations with LLM agents raise questions about how well they represent real human or agent behaviour. A contest was confirmed only for NeurIPS 2024. Not to be confused with Concordia AI, the Beijing organisation on the aisafety.com map.

Eon Systems PBC Bridge

Company · San Francisco, USA · founded 2024

A San Francisco public-benefit corporation, founded by Michael Andregg, that is building whole-brain emulations from connectomics, expansion microscopy and functional imaging, under the mission 'brain emulation so humans can flourish in a world with superintelligence'. In March 2026 it announced what it called the first embodied emulation of an adult fruit fly brain (about 139,000 neurons and 50 million connections) controlling a simulated body, a claim critics disputed as not yet a true 'upload'. The brain model builds on a 2024 Nature model by its head of engineering, Philip Shiu, and colleagues. Eon raised a $3.5M seed round, led by Protocol Labs, in December 2025.

It offers brain emulation as an alternative, possibly more legible, path to general intelligence, and pitches it as a way for humans to keep pace with superintelligence. It is a concrete test case for int/a's 'speed of wisdom' question: does emulation help safety, or add another race?

Works on Agency, Power · Key work Embodied whole-brain emulation of an adult fruit fly in a simulated body (2026); A Drosophila computational brain model reveals sensorimotor processing (Shiu et al., Nature) (2024); $3.5M seed round led by Protocol Labs (2025) · Get involved Careers page on eon.systems; about six roles listed on Simplify in 2026; 'Partner with Eon' contact on its homepage

Note It is contested whether whole-brain emulation helps safety or simply opens another capabilities race. At the time of announcement, the embodied fly result had not been released for independent checking (The Decoder). The neuron model is a simple threshold model, and reported neuron counts vary (125k-139k). Press calls Wissner-Gross a co-founder; the site lists him as founding advisor. The founding year comes from a jobs aggregator. Emulations would also raise digital-minds welfare questions, which Eon does not discuss publicly.

Foresight Institute: AI safety grants and AI for Science & Safety Nodes (incl. neurotechnology for safe AI) BridgeOn aisafety.comChanged

Funder · San Francisco, United States · founded 2023 · also draws on Safety science, Formal

The AI-safety grant programme of Foresight Institute, a San Francisco nonprofit founded in 1986 around nanotechnology and long-range technology. Since 2023 it has funded work on security, privacy, decentralised cooperation, epistemics and neurotechnology. Its neurotech line funds brain-computer interfaces, whole brain emulation and 'lo-fi' emulation as routes to human-aligned intelligence. In November 2025 the programme was restructured into the 'AI for Science & Safety Nodes', which combine grants (mostly $30k to $100k), compute and office space in San Francisco and Berlin, with whole brain emulation now under an 'AI-first Science: Bio, Neuro, Nano' call.

It is one of very few funders that treat neurotechnology (BCI, whole brain emulation) as an AI-safety strategy rather than a medical or capabilities goal. Its Berlin node puts a funded AI-safety hub with compute within reach of int/a's Berlin community.

Levin Lab and Allen Discovery Center at Tufts University Bridge

Academic · Medford, MA, USA · founded 2016 · also draws on AI minds

Michael Levin's developmental-biology lab at Tufts and the Allen Discovery Center he directs. They study bioelectricity, morphogenesis, synthetic organisms and 'diverse intelligence' in cells, tissues, robots and software. In 2025-26 the lab posted a steady stream of AI preprints. Two 2026 preprints treat AI alignment directly: one proposes homeostatic objectives for AI by analogy with cancer as cellular misalignment, the other argues that decentralised systems align to a 'virtual governor'.

It offers a biological account of how competent parts align into larger selves, and of how they defect, as in cancer, as well as frameworks (TAME, cognitive light cones) for detecting goals in unfamiliar systems. The AI-safety field rarely draws on either. It is now applying these ideas to multi-agent alignment and AI objectives.

Works on Agency, Multi-agent, AI status · Key work Alignment Is to a Virtual Governor: A Theory of Coordination in Diverse Intelligence (2026); From Cancer to AI Alignment: Tackling Externalities Through Homeostatic Principles (2026); Diverse Intelligence: an essential field for questions of AI and Consciousness (2025) · Get involved Research positions through the lab and Tufts (check drmichaellevin.org)

Note AI is a growing strand, not the lab's main business, which is regenerative medicine and morphogenesis. The alignment papers are preprints. Levin's broader metaphysical claims about minds (e.g. 'ingressing minds') are contested. The lab predates the 2016 centre (Levin has been at Tufts since 2009); the founding year given is the centre's. Scale is an estimate.

Neuromatch (incl. AI Sentience Scholars) Bridge

Nonprofit · Distributed · founded 2020 · also draws on AI minds

A global US 501(c)(3), founded in 2020, that runs online academies in computational neuroscience, deep learning, NeuroAI, computational behaviour and climate science. It reports 13,217 students from 137 countries and a community of 30,000+ including TAs and volunteers. It also runs the Impact Scholars research programme (204 scholars since 2023) and MEXA, a Wellcome-funded community on generative AI for mental health. In 2026 it launched AI Sentience Scholars: a six-month, part-time, Longview-funded programme in which ten early-career researchers apply neuroscience methods to AI sentience. It was developed with PRISM, Cambridge Digital Minds and the Institute of Neuroethics, and its scientific director is Megan Peters.

It is the largest training pipeline for computational neuroscience and NeuroAI, and AI Sentience Scholars brings empirical consciousness-science methods such as metacognition and psychophysics to AI welfare. Its mentors include Steve Fleming, Axel Cleeremans and Susan Schneider. A NeuroAI-for-safety track would fit the same infrastructure but does not exist yet.

NOOMA Labs (successor to Cross Labs) BridgeChanged

Nonprofit · Kyoto, Japan · founded 2026 · also draws on Formal

NOOMA Labs is an independent research lab that Olaf Witkowski is setting up in Kyoto, in partnership with Foundry Labs. It continues the programme of Cross Labs, the institute funded by Cross Compass that he directed from 2019 until it closed on 31 August 2026. It studies which principles of intelligence carry across living and artificial systems: agency and open-ended learning, collective intelligence, cognition and consciousness, and embodiment. Its highlighted output is a 2026 PNAS Nexus paper, written with Hector Zenil and others, arguing that full alignment is unattainable and that a diverse ecosystem of mutually influencing AI agents is a safer target.

It brings artificial-life and open-endedness research, which studies intelligence as emergent and embodied, to alignment questions. It argues for diversity and balance among agents rather than control. Through Witkowski it also links the Japanese ALife community to CSAS's contemplative alignment work.

Whole Brain Architecture Initiative (WBAI) Bridge

Nonprofit · Tokyo, Japan · founded 2015

A Tokyo-based specified nonprofit, founded in 2015 and chaired by Hiroshi Yamakawa, that promotes building AGI from the architecture of the whole human brain under the motto 'Let's build a brain together'. It maintains Brain Reference Architecture data and tools (BRAES, WholeBIF, CoBRAC), runs hackathons, tutorials, international workshops and a small incentive award, and aims to finish an alpha Whole-Brain Reference Architecture by early 2027. Since its 2026 New Year message it has presented brain-like AGI as a 'bridge' between humanity and superintelligence: a mediator that understands human values from experience and conveys them, while offering an independent reference point for verification.

It holds a distinctively Japanese thesis: human-like, brain-structured AGI could make AI internals legible and act as a translator of human values to superintelligence. This links to Yamakawa's ALIGN network and its post-singularity symbiosis work.

World Academy of Art and Science (WAAS) Bridge

Membership body · Napa, USA · founded 1960 · also draws on Arts, futures, Peace

An academy of more than 560 elected fellows from over 90 countries, founded in 1960 by figures including Robert Oppenheimer, Bertrand Russell and Joseph Needham. It is registered in Napa, California, and holds UN ECOSOC consultative status. Its AI work runs mainly through EXTRA (Existential Threats and Risks to All), a working group set up in 2022 that keeps a directory of several hundred existential-risk reports, issues a monthly newsletter and co-hosts symposia, treating AI and artificial superintelligence alongside climate, nuclear, pandemic and ecological threats as parts of one polycrisis. It also lists an AI Governance project under its 'Technology as Force for Good' programme.

EXTRA reads AI risk as one strand of a systemic polycrisis rather than in isolation, and convenes voices outside the Anglophone AI-safety community, for example an October 2026 Beijing symposium on existential-risk governance with the Centre for China and Globalisation. It is a ready-made network of senior scholars for the 'AI within the metacrisis' framing int/a holds, though its output is mostly curation and convening rather than original research.

Works on Metacrisis, Epistemics · Key work EXTRA InfoHub, directory of existential-risk reports and monthly eNewsletter (e.g. Oct 2025 issue 'Artificial Intelligence: Between Threat and Promise') (2022); Symposium 'Synthetic Societies: Human Vulnerability and Systemic Fragility in a Context of Rising Algorithmic Power' (with CIRET) (2026); Symposium 'Global Existential Risk Governance for Human Survival: Chinese Perspectives on Enhancing Cooperation' (with CCG, Beijing, 15 Oct 2026) (2026) · Get involved EXTRA monthly eNewsletter (free subscription); Live-streamed EXTRA symposia and WAAS webinars, e.g. the hybrid Beijing symposium on existential-risk governance, 15 Oct 2026; Events can be submitted to EXTRA's events listing

Its October 2026 partner, the Centre for China and Globalisation, was founded by a former State Council counsellor.

AI for Collective Intelligence Research Hub (AI4CI) Adjacent

Programme · Bristol, UK · founded 2024 · also draws on Democracy

UKRI-funded National AI Research Hub (EPSRC grant EP/Y028392/1, Feb 2024 to Jan 2029). It is led from the University of Bristol with Bath, Cardiff, Exeter, Glasgow, UCL and Ulster and more than 40 stakeholder partners. It develops AI that gathers and makes sense of distributed data and supports collective decision-making in healthcare, finance, the environment, pandemics and cities, with cross-cutting themes on human-centred design and governance infrastructure. It holds complex-systems and agent-based modelling know-how about how communities of people and AI agents behave together. That knowledge bears on multi-agent and gradual-disempowerment questions, though the hub treats AI as a tool for collective intelligence rather than a risk to it.

ANU School of Cybernetics Adjacent

Academic · Canberra, Australia · founded 2021 · also draws on Law, society, Arts, futures

A school of the Australian National University, founded in 2021 by Genevieve Bell, that re-establishes cybernetics as an applied discipline for 'navigating major societal transformations'. It runs a one-year Master of Applied Cybernetics, a cohort-based PhD programme, short courses and the Cybernetic Imagination Residency. Its AI work includes the 'AI Adoption in Australia' survey with Google (2026), 'LLMs Unplugged' AI-literacy workshops for schools, public servants and academics, and art-and-AI projects.

It is one of the few institutions training practitioners to treat AI as one component of socio-technical systems, using the cybernetics tradition (Beer, Bateson, second-order cybernetics) that mainstream AI safety rarely draws on. That makes it a natural partner for systems-level AI governance and public AI-literacy work.

Works on Epistemics, Metacrisis · Key work AI Adoption in Australia (with Google): national survey of 3,500+ adults on generative AI use and governance expectations (2026); LLMs Unplugged / My First LLM: computer-free AI-literacy workshops (2025); Master of Applied Cybernetics (reaccredited for five years in 2025) (2025) · Get involved Master of Applied Cybernetics: in-person, Canberra, February to November cohort (2026 indicative fees AUD 39,925 domestic, AUD 56,120 international); Cohort-based PhD programme; Cybernetic Imagination Residency for artists and thinkers
