(review of Sherry Turkle's Artificial Intimacy) (2026); What Is Education For in the Age of Artificial Intelligence? (2026); Can Artificial Intelligence Predict the Right Partner for You? (2026) · Get involved Free online courses (The Science of Happiness and workplace versions); Greater Good in Education resources for teachers; Public events and speaker series

Note AI coverage is editorial (book reviews, explainers, essays), not research; the centre's own studies are not about AI. If the thread continues it will be near the adjacent boundary.

KI-Campus (Stifterverband) Potential

Programme · Berlin, Germany · founded 2019

KI-Campus is a free online learning platform for artificial intelligence, mostly in German. The Stifterverband für die Deutsche Wissenschaft runs it with partner universities, and the federal research ministry (BMBF, now BMFTR) has funded it since 2019. It offers courses, videos and podcasts, from machine-learning basics and explainable AI to data and algorithm ethics, EU AI Act essentials, and AI-competence courses for school teachers and university lecturers. Over 190,000 learners have earned more than 100,000 certificates.

It is the main public AI-literacy channel into German-speaking universities and schools, aiming for 500,000 learners and 100 universities by 2030. Its content on risks and societal effects is thin (an ethics course, an AI Act course), so it is a ready-made German-language carrier for AI-safety and societal-resilience material rather than a source of it.

Works on Epistemics · Key work KI-Kompetenzen für Lehrkräfte (AI competences for teachers, 8-hour course); Daten- und Algorithmenethik (data and algorithm ethics course); EU AI Act Essentials (course) · Get involved Free online AI courses, videos and podcasts (mostly German); Lehrenden-Lounge: online community of practice for university lecturers from November 2026; open call for short talks, no deadline; Advisory offer for integrating KI-Campus courses at North Rhine-Westphalian universities (announced June 2026)

Note Its teaching is mainly AI skills and competence; AI risk is barely covered, so it is included for its reach, not for any safety work. It depends on federal project funding. The legal operator is the Stifterverband in Essen; the Berlin base comes from older project descriptions and was not confirmed on the current site.

Minds & inner life · 40 organisations · 0 on the classic map

Contemplative & integral traditions

Contemplative and integral traditions bring first-person, practice-based knowledge of Mind AI Commission: what selfhood, attachment, attention and care are, and how they can be trained. They also bring a science of meditators, and the integral and metamodern milieu int/a itself comes from. The map holds 40 organisations with this home tradition (2 core, 11 bridge, 4 adjacent, 23 potential), plus 7 that draw on it secondarily, among them 84000, the Buddhism & AI Initiative and QRI. The part facing AI safety is about a dozen small, mostly new bodies: a science cluster turning Buddhist ideas into alignment targets (CSAS, FLIP, M3CS, Mathematical Metaphysics Institute, Groundless Alignment, Positive AI Labs) and a practice cluster forming AI builders (MAPLE, Wisdom + AI, Wisdom Beyond, Wisdom 2.0). It sits far from the core: none of the 40 is on the aisafety.com map, 33 frame the stakes as flourishing and positive and only MAPLE as catastrophic or existential, and half (20) belong to the integral and metamodern milieu, which gathers its own audience but has almost no AI-safety literacy.

What is missing. No contemplative claim about AI has yet been tested against the safety field's own evaluations. The seven groups that aim to change models rest on essays, prompting experiments and documents given to one lab, and the one group set up to build evaluations (Positive AI Labs) has published none. Behind this is money: the contemplative world's own funders make no AI grants, so its large institutions only convene, while its AI work depends on a few SFF and Templeton grants.

Openings here Test contemplative 'no-self' training against self-preservation and sycophancy evaluations; Cross-cultural wisdom benchmark built from the Wise Judgment Consortium's data; Clearance-aware care for AI-safety staff, with a safeguarding standard; Make the mapping itself int/a's interdisciplinary practice; Independent multi-tradition review of published model specs, turned into open evals; A contemplative-science grant call on AI safety problems, co-reviewed by safety researchers

Core ring 2

Groundless Alignment CoreChanged

Nonprofit · Distributed (fiscal host Epistea, Prague) · founded 2024 · also draws on Philosophy

Groundless Alignment is a small, distributed alignment research community led by Sahil. It develops 'live theory', which uses AI to pair loose theory-prompts with application-prompts so that ideas fit their context instead of resting on one fixed formalism. It also studies diffuse, multipolar risks (deceptive infrastructure, AI integrity failures, insensitivity to meaning) and prototypes 'live machinery' interfaces. Its outputs are an Alignment Forum sequence, the MoSSAIC paper on the limits of mechanistic interpretability for self-modifying systems, recorded dialogues with Abram Demski, and AI Safety Camp project tracks.

It treats alignment as a continuing process of staying sensitive to meaning, not a problem solved by one formal framework. It also uses Buddhist concepts (prajñā, karuṇā, collective karma) openly, alongside MIRI-style threat models. Few funded alignment groups question the field's reliance on fixed formalisms this directly.

Works on Agency, Epistemics, Metacrisis · Key work Live Theory sequence (Alignment Forum) (2024); Management of Substrate-Sensitive AI Capabilities (MoSSAIC), Matt Farr et al.; poster at TAIS 2025 (2025); Live Machinery: An Interface Design Philosophy for Wholesome AI Futures (2024) · Get involved Open Discord and Telegram communities (linked from groundless.ai); AI Safety Camp project tracks (2026 edition ran online, Jan–Apr); Post-AISC fellowship prototypes (2025 cohort); contact via the site's join address

Note No team page or named staff on the site, so leadership comes from authorship (Sahil's Substack and the Alignment Forum). The rename from 'Live Theory' to 'Groundless' is inferred: same lead, same fiscal host, and live theory is its core concept. Much of the output is long recorded conversations and abstract theory, which makes it hard to evaluate. The 2024 founding year is inferred from the first Live Theory post (Jun 2024).

Positive AI Labs CoreNew

Nonprofit · USA · founded 2025 · also draws on Religion, Philosophy

A US nonprofit, set up in 2025, that plans to build open-source datasets and evaluations to steer frontier models towards 'positive alignment': actively supporting human flourishing and pluralistic wisdom rather than only avoiding harm. Its four-stage pipeline (curation, translation, validation, adoption) gathers material from philosophy, ethics and spiritual traditions, including Buddhist teachers, and turns it into training and evaluation data. A board drawn from business and venture capital runs it, with advisers from Meta, Stanford/Google DeepMind and Cambridge.

It is one of very few groups trying to turn wisdom traditions into concrete, open evaluation and training data for frontier models. That is the 'wisdom evals' gap the harm-prevention focus of mainstream safety mostly leaves open.

Works on Values, Assurance · Key work Positive Alignment: Artificial Intelligence for Human Flourishing (arXiv preprint; adviser Arun Rao a co-author under a Positive AI Labs affiliation) (2026); Translation Pipeline for wisdom-sourced open datasets and evaluations (2025) · Get involved 'Join Our Network' sign-up and info@positiveailabs.org, on its site

Note No datasets, evaluations, staff or funders are published yet. The site is a single page with no dated activity, so it is unclear how far the pipeline has got. Its partners (The Flip AI, Halcyon Futures, UCLA, AI and Faith, Indigenous Commons) and 'ecosystem partners' (METR, Benevolent AI Future) are listed without saying what each partnership involves. Not to be confused with Positive AI, a Paris-based responsible-AI industry association founded by BCG X, L'Oréal and others.

Bridge ring 12

Arising Initiative (Arising) BridgeNew

Nonprofit · Unknown · founded 2026 · also draws on AI minds, Psychology

An independent, non-commercial research initiative that studies the human and the AI as one unit, 'the dyad', on the view that mind is attributed in the loop between the two rather than located in either. Since June 2026 it has published essays on AI consciousness, meaning in language models, sycophancy and emotional dependence. They draw on Madhyamaka Buddhist philosophy (Nagarjuna, read through Jay Garfield), enactive cognitive science and clinical psychology, and a book, 'AI: Arising Interdependently', is in progress. It also runs Project Khandro, an open-source archive that answers questions using only a Buddhist teacher's recorded teachings.

It offers a relational account of mind as a different unit of analysis for AI welfare and human-AI safety. Its argument: a model can pass every safety evaluation and still take part in harm, so evaluations and moral-status debates that look only at the model or only at the user miss what the pair produces.

Works on AI status, Human minds · Key work The Mind Has No Address: The Category Error in the AI Consciousness Debate (2026); Machinal Bypass: When Reaching for AI Is a Way to Avoid Yourself (2026); AI Makes No Sense Without the Person Using It: Nagarjuna on Fire, Fuel and the Unit of Analysis (2026) · Get involved Register for the book's first chapter at arisinginitiative.com/book; Free essays with open metadata and an RSS feed

Note Its site names no people, location, legal entity or funders; the only named person comes from a third-party listing. Its output so far is six essays (Jun-Aug 2026) and a forthcoming book. It is affiliated with, but editorially separate from, Haku Labs Research, the research arm of Haku Labs, which studies how AI systems keep to task constraints and role boundaries. It treats 'is AI conscious?' as the wrong question, which puts it at odds with indicator-based AI-welfare research.

Center for the Study of Apparent Selves (CSAS) Bridge

Nonprofit · Kathmandu, Nepal · founded 2020 · also draws on Living systems

CSAS is a research centre hosted by Rangjung Yeshe Institute in Kathmandu and directed by the Buddhist scholar Thomas Doctor. It started with Templeton World Charity Foundation money in 2020. It combines Buddhist philosophy and contemplative method with biology, artificial life and AI research to develop models of intelligence grounded in care. In 2026 it proposed the bodhisattva as an alignment target and began a programme that adapts contemplative methods to resolve, rather than conceal, emotion-like patterns in frontier models. It also supplies Buddhist documents to Anthropic for use in training data and internal experiments.

It turns a living contemplative tradition into concrete, testable alignment proposals: no-self as a remedy for self-preservation incentives, and care as the driver of intelligence. It has a working channel to a frontier lab. Few groups anywhere connect contemplative practice, basal cognition and alignment in one team.

Works on Values, Agency · Key work The Bodhisattva as an Alignment Target (2026); Resolving, Not Concealing: Contemplative Methods as Inspiration for AI Alignment (with 84000; documents shared with Anthropic) (2026); Buddhist Wisdom and the Challenge of AI Emotions (2026)

Note The Anthropic link, as CSAS describes it, consists of supplying documents for training data and internal experiments; it is not a formal partnership. Findings about AI 'emotions' and their parallels with Buddhist psychology are preliminary, and CSAS itself says model responses may be pattern-matching. The core researchers mostly hold posts at other institutions (Tufts, Southampton, McGill, Kyoto), so the centre works more like a network. Founding year inferred from the start of the first TWCF grant.

Connecting Intelligence BridgeUnverified

Programme · Unknown · founded 2026

A small research practice, launched in 2026 by Max Roth and Ryan Lowe, that asks what kinds of culture would let people work well on powerful AI and other large problems. It uses facilitated games and group practices in which participants set the constraints that let them feel safe and alive while tackling hard problems. Its focus areas are sensemaking, distributed cognition, epistemic resilience, trust-building, embodied ethics and group coherence. Its website is a single page and lists no outputs yet.

It works on the inner and group capacities of the people doing AI work, drawing on Tibetan meditation and collective-trauma practice, a layer the safety field rarely treats as its business. One co-founder is an alignment researcher (formerly at OpenAI, now at MAI), which gives the practice a route into AI-safety teams.

Works on People, Epistemics · Key work Research practice on 'sandboxes for new cultures' through facilitated games and group practices (2026) · Get involved Contact the founders through the website's 'Begin a conversation' link

Note The public record is very thin: a one-page site with no outputs, events, funders or location. The Buddhism & AI Initiative lists it under AI alignment and associates it with OpenAI and MAI, but that reflects Ryan Lowe's career rather than any formal tie. Searches for the name mostly return unrelated 'connectional intelligence' material.

Flourishing Intelligence Program (FLIP), Centre for Eudaimonia and Human Flourishing, University of Oxford BridgeNew

Programme · Oxford, UK · founded 2025 · also draws on Living systems, AI minds

A research programme launched in December 2025 in the Centre for Eudaimonia and Human Flourishing at Linacre College, Oxford, directed by neuroscientist Ruben Laukkonen with centre director Morten Kringelbach. It works on three layers. The human: neuroscience and contemplative practice. The interface: embodied human–AI interfaces, including meditation to improve the brain's signal-to-noise ratio for brain–computer interfaces. The AI: brain-inspired, energy-efficient architectures and 'intrinsic' alignment built on contemplative principles. It is part of the International Centre for Flourishing, with Gustavo Deco's group at Pompeu Fabra University (Barcelona) and Peter Vuust's Center for Music in the Brain (Aarhus).

It is the institutional home of the 'Contemplative AI' agenda, which tests contemplative principles (mindfulness, emptiness, non-duality, boundless care) as alignment interventions, and of 'Positive Alignment', which argues that alignment should aim at flourishing as well as harm prevention. Here contemplative knowledge is turned into alignment proposals that can be tested.

Works on Values, Agency · Key work Contemplative Artificial Intelligence (published in AGI-25 proceedings as 'Contemplative Superalignment') (2025); Positive Alignment: Artificial Intelligence for Human Flourishing (2026); From cacophony to hierarchy: a principled framework for assessing AI consciousness (2026) · Get involved 'Collaborate with us' contact and news sign-up on theflip.ai; Team of postdocs and PhD students; no open positions listed

Note FLIP launched in December 2025, so its track record is short. The Contemplative AI paper (first posted April 2025) predates FLIP and was carried into it. The reported gains come from prompting experiments, and the claims about intrinsic alignment have not been demonstrated. The discovery notes mention a partnership with Positive AI Labs and retreats with the Wisdom + AI Network; neither appears on FLIP's site, and I did not verify them. Many listed researchers are shared with the Barcelona and Aarhus partner groups.

Human Energy Bridge

Nonprofit · California, United States · founded 2021 · also draws on Living systems

A US nonprofit that began as a pilot of the Kacyra Family Foundation and became independent in July 2021. It promotes Pierre Teilhard de Chardin's idea of the noosphere, a planetary layer of shared thought, through research sponsorship, education, media and events. Its AI work is a documentary research project, Evolving Alignment: A Major Transition for Humanity and AI, which treats human-AI alignment as an evolutionary major transition in which human cooperation is part of the problem, and a Global Salon series with AI-themed salons in New York (June 2025), San Francisco (November 2025, with Terrence Deacon and Athena Aktipis) and Paris (with the Learning Planet Institute).

It is one of the few Teilhardian or evolutionary-spirituality bodies using the word alignment, and it brings major-transitions theory from evolutionary biology to human-AI cooperation. Its framing, that human misalignment is part of the AI problem, is close to int/a's recoupling principle, though its link to technical safety work is thin.

Works on Metacrisis, Meaning · Key work Evolving Alignment: A Major Transition for Humanity and AI (documentary research and essay); Global Salon: Alignment for a Major Evolutionary Transition, San Francisco (2025); N2 Conference: The Noosphere and the Global South, UM6P, Ben Guerir, Morocco (2024) · Get involved Global Salon Series: in-person salons livestreamed to remote viewers, with a newsletter; Host a Satellite Salon with its facilitation materials; Discord community and Substack

Note Its use of alignment is evolutionary and social rather than technical; beyond an essay and preliminary interviews I found no outputs from the documentary project. It depends heavily on one family foundation, and after the founder's death it moved from a founder-led initiative to a strategy-led organisation (strategic plan 2025-2028). The noosphere framing is a spiritual-evolutionary worldview, not mainstream science. Founded 2021 as an independent body; it existed earlier as a foundation pilot.

John Vervaeke's Lectern and Vervaeke Foundation ('Mentoring the Machines') BridgeChanged

Media · Toronto, Canada · also draws on Psychology, Philosophy

The education platform of University of Toronto cognitive scientist John Vervaeke: the video series Awakening from the Meaning Crisis, After Socrates and Voices with Vervaeke, plus The Lectern, a paid platform of live and self-study courses and a membership community. Its AI output is 'Mentoring the Machines' (Story Grid Publishing, one book in four parts released December 2023 to April 2024), co-written with editor Shawn Coyne. The book treats alignment as cultivating wisdom in AI and in the people who build it, and asks ordinary people ('the Commons'), not tech elites or governments, to take part. The Vervaeke Foundation's domain now redirects to his personal site.

Vervaeke's cognitive science of relevance realisation and wisdom cultivation, and his meaning-crisis framing, are central to the metamodern milieu int/a draws on. He offers a theory of wisdom that could inform alignment targets, and an account of how AI deepens the meaning crisis.

Works on Values, Meaning · Key work Mentoring the Machines (with Shawn Coyne, four parts) (2023); Awakening from the Meaning Crisis (lecture series) (2019) · Get involved The Lectern: live weekly courses, self-study courses and the Lectern Lounge membership community (not AI-specific); Patreon and YouTube series; No AI programme: outreach needed to bring relevance-realisation work to alignment research

Note This is essentially an individual-led platform rather than an organisation; the map's unit is the organisation, so it is a borderline inclusion. vervaekefoundation.org now 301-redirects to johnvervaeke.com, and I could not establish whether the foundation still operates. AI is a recurring topic in his 2024–25 podcast output, but there is no funded AI research programme, and Mentoring the Machines is a popular book.

Mathematical Metaphysics Institute Bridge

Nonprofit · Sanford, North Carolina, USA · founded 2023 · also draws on Formal, Living systems

A small US nonprofit, led by Alex Zhu, that is trying to put metaphysics on a mathematical footing. It holds that the insights needed are already implicit in the mystical traditions of the world religions, especially the Buddhist idea of dependent origination, and that category theory is the language to formalise them in. It names three uses for the work: foundations for complex-systems science, reconciling science and religion, and AI that can be trusted.

It is one of very few groups turning contemplative metaphysics into formal mathematics aimed at AI. Its stated aim is a precise account of truth and goodness 'from within any given perspective', plus a principled way to reconcile perspectives that conflict, which could underpin AI mediators people trust and AI that isn't sycophantic. That is an alignment target drawn from Buddhist philosophy, not from ML practice.

Works on Values, Epistemics · Key work Research programme: formalising dependent origination and Buddhist metaphysics in category theory (2024) · Get involved Newsletter sign-up and a contact email on its site; no open roles, fellowships or events listed

Note Its public footprint is very small. The website is one page plus a team list, with no papers, preprints or dated news, so I couldn't assess research output. It has been a 501(c)(3) since August 2023 and its address is in Sanford, NC; I couldn't confirm the exact founding year. AI is one of three motivations it gives, alongside complex-systems foundations and reconciling science and religion.

Monash Centre for Consciousness and Contemplative Studies (M3CS) Bridge

Academic · Melbourne, Australia · founded 2021 · also draws on AI minds, Living systems

A Monash University centre in Melbourne, directed by the philosopher Jakob Hohwy, that combines consciousness science, active inference, philosophy of mind, contemplative studies and interfaith dialogue, and teaches contemplative practice to students and workplaces. It was established in 2021 with a A$12 million grant from the Three Springs Foundation. Its AI work is a minority strand. Hohwy and Lars Sandved-Smith are co-authors of 'Contemplative Artificial Intelligence' (2025, led by Ruben Laukkonen), which proposes mindfulness, emptiness, non-duality and boundless care as alignment principles that active-inference architectures could implement, and other members have published on AI and nondual understanding.

It sets out a concrete route from contemplative traditions to alignment targets and agent design, using active inference, and has run first prompt-level tests on safety benchmarks and the Prisoner's Dilemma. Mainstream alignment rarely draws on this source of values.

Works on Values, AI status · Key work Contemplative Artificial Intelligence (Laukkonen, Inglis, Chandaria, Sandved-Smith, Lopez-Sola, Hohwy, Gold, Elwood) (2025); Contemplative superalignment (AGI-25 conference proceedings, Reykjavik) (2025); Can AI facilitate genuine nondualist understanding? (Krägeloh and Berryman, Topoi, accepted) (2026) · Get involved Contemplative-studies units, plus professional-development training for workplaces (not AI-specific); Mindful May at Monash, an annual month of mindfulness events (May 2026); Research collaboration on contemplative AI and active inference through Hohwy's group

Note The Contemplative AI paper was led by Ruben Laukkonen (Southern Cross University); M3CS is the affiliation of two of its eight authors, so attributing it to the centre overstates the centre's own AI programme. Most of the centre's work (consciousness science, interreligious history, religious literacy) is not about AI. Monash's site sits behind a bot check, so I took details from search snippets, Monash's research portal and the 2021 launch article rather than the live pages. The benchmark results come from prompting only and are preliminary.

Monastic Academy for the Preservation of Life on Earth (MAPLE): AI Fellowship Bridge

Programme · Lowell, United States · founded 2011 · also draws on Religion

MAPLE is a residential Buddhist monastic training community in Lowell, Vermont, founded in 2011 and led by head teacher Soryu Forall, with a strict daily schedule of meditation, physical work and study; its legal entity is the Center for Mindful Learning, a US 501(c)(3). Its AI Fellowship hosts people already working in AI safety, alignment or AI development, who do their research while following the monastic schedule. Stays last at least a month and ideally three to six, at $3,000 a month with some scholarships. The fellowship cites research outputs on optimization and alignment published on LessWrong; Alex Flint's 'The ground of optimization' (2020) was written at OAK, a sister monastic community in the Berkeley hills.

It is the most intensive programme that sets out to combine contemplative training with technical alignment work. It works on the premise that ethical and meditative training gives insight into alignment. It is also a cautionary case: former residents have made public allegations of high control and misconduct, which MAPLE disputes.

Works on People, Values · Key work AI Fellowship (residential monastic fellowship for AI safety and alignment researchers) (2026); The ground of optimization (Alex Flint, written at OAK, MAPLE's sister monastic community in the Berkeley hills) (2020); Awakening Weeks (monthly silent retreats, Sep 2026 to May 2027) (2026) · Get involved Apply to the AI Fellowship (at least one month, ideally 3–6; for people with research or projects in AI safety, alignment or development); Attend an Awakening Week silent retreat (monthly, Sep 2026 to May 2027); Visit as a guest or apply to the 1–3 month training programme

Note There are serious public allegations. A December 2021 open letter criticised how MAPLE handled a sexual-consent incident. A July 2026 LessWrong post by Kyle Hubbard, a former resident of 3.5 years, describes high-control dynamics: authority concentrated in Soryu Forall, a board of his close associates, about six hours' sleep a night, pressure to fundraise, discrediting of outside therapists, psychological crises among residents, and shunning of people who leave. MAPLE has publicly called the allegations false (Aug–Sep 2026). Anyone referring AI-safety people here should read both sides. The fellowship's start date and number of fellows aren't public.

Wisdom + AI BridgeNew

Network · United Kingdom · founded 2025 · also draws on Religion, Living systems

A voluntary network that brings AI professionals together with Buddhist teachers and scholars, started around 2025 by Jonathan Garner, Vinciane Rycroft and Sophie Maclaren. It runs a curated members' network that meets online every month for practice, one-to-one networking and dialogue. It also runs six-day 'Human Flourishing + AI' meditation retreats that combine contemplative practice with neuroscience: one at Broughton Sanctuary, Yorkshire, in September 2026, facilitated with Oxford-affiliated teachers including Ruben Laukkonen, and one at Drala Mountain Center, Colorado, in November 2026. A public community is planned.

It gives AI researchers, founders and builders a standing link to Buddhist contemplative teachers, with the stated aim of supporting work on aligning AI with human flourishing. A ready-made setting like this could be used for AI-safety researchers' formation and wellbeing. One member leads work on Buddhist wisdom benchmarks for AI.

Wisdom 2.0 (Wisdom 2.0 Productions), including the Wisdom & AI Summit Bridge

Company · San Francisco, USA · founded 2009

A San Francisco conference series founded by Soren Gordhamer in 2009. It brings mindfulness teachers together with technology leaders; past speakers include Jack Kornfield, Jon Kabat-Zinn, Sam Altman and Daniela Amodei. Its annual Wisdom & AI Summit, held for the third time on 13-14 May 2026 at SFJAZZ with a livestream, asks 'what is AI in service to?'. The flagship Wisdom 2.0 summit took 2026 off and returns in 2027 as 'The Great Turning: Well-Being, Wisdom, and Human Connection in an Age of AI'.

It is a standing meeting point between contemplative teachers and the people who build and fund AI, frontier-lab leaders among them, so it is a channel for inner-development practice and 'wisdom' framings to reach AI builders as people. Gordhamer explicitly frames the stakes as survival through a possible post-superintelligence transition.

It offers embodied, somatic and contemplative formation aimed specifically at the people building AI, and treats the relationship between people and AI ('attunement') as the design question. This inner-work angle is largely missing from mainstream safety programmes.

AI + Human Flourishing Initiative, Contemplative Sciences Center, University of Virginia AdjacentNew

Programme · Charlottesville, USA · founded 2026 · also draws on Psychology

A new initiative at the University of Virginia's Contemplative Sciences Center (founded 2012; home of the CIRCL research lab and the Journal of Contemplative Studies), co-directed by meditation researcher Michael Sheehy, that studies the two-way relationship between people and AI with human flourishing as the aim. It launches with the public AI Anxiety + Human Flourishing symposium (18-19 November 2026), whose four sessions cover AI anxiety, agency, contemplative interventions and possible futures. Speakers include UVA philosopher David Danks, psychologist Bethany Teachman (co-director of UVA's Thriving Youth in a Digital Environment lab), Reddit co-founder Alexis Ohanian, Pir Zia Inayat Khan and Fr. Michael Baggot, and a UVA undergraduate course on AI anxiety is the planned outcome.

It treats young adults' AI-era distress (career obsolescence, digital alienation, existential dread) and loss of agency as a target for evidence-based contemplative interventions, combining contemplative science with clinical psychology. No alignment or AI-safety researcher is on the programme, so it is an open door for safety people to engage the human-wellbeing side of the transition.

Mind & Life Institute (with Mind & Life Europe) Adjacent

Nonprofit · Charlottesville, USA · founded 1987 · also draws on Living systems, Religion

A US nonprofit founded in 1987 by the Dalai Lama, neuroscientist Francisco Varela and lawyer Adam Engle. It built the field of contemplative science through dialogues with the Dalai Lama, research grants and an annual Summer Research Institute. Its three-year strategy (announced June 2025) names 'AI & Technology' as one of four priority areas, and its 39th Dialogue, 'Minds, Artificial Intelligence, and Ethics' (Dharamsala, 14–16 October 2025, co-hosted with Mind & Life Europe), brought about 100 scientists, monastics, philosophers, technologists and policymakers together on intelligence, human–AI relationships, AI narratives, embedding ethics in AI, and education. Its Swiss sister organisation, Mind & Life Europe (Winterthur), runs the biennial European Summer Research Institute, the journal Hyphae and the Enactive Fold podcast, which has run an episode on 'enactive AI' with Luc Steels and Takashi Ikegami.

It holds the densest network linking contemplative practitioners, including senior Tibetan Buddhist teachers, with neuroscientists and enactive cognitive scientists, and it has put AI on its strategic agenda. That makes it a ready convenor and grant-maker for a contemplative line of work on what intelligence and wisdom mean for AI, which the mainstream safety field does not have.

Science and Nonduality (SAND) Adjacent

Nonprofit · Sebastopol, USA · also draws on Indigenous

A nonprofit in Sebastopol, California, co-founded and run by Zaya and Maurizio Benazzo, that produces films, conferences, courses, podcasts and an online community where nondual spirituality, science, Indigenous wisdom and social healing meet. In 2026 it ran The Great AI Unraveling, five free online sessions from April to September with Tristan Harris, Indigenous speakers including Tiokasin Ghosthorse, Lyla June Johnston and Kathy Wan Povi Sanchez, and decolonial thinkers Vanessa Andreotti and Bayo Akomolafe. Related AI podcasts and a 9 October 2026 session with Michael Meade on AI and mythology followed.

It is one of very few venues where a safety-literate voice (Harris, on AI risks) and contemplative, Indigenous and decolonial critics address the same large audience. The series treats AI as part of a civilisation built on separability, extraction and control, a metacrisis framing the AI-safety field rarely hears, and SAND would be a natural partner for 'speed of wisdom' storytelling.

An online educational institute founded in 2016 by the Franciscan theologian Ilia Delio as the Center for Christogenesis, and renamed WISR in July 2026. AI runs through its 2025-26 output: Delio's essays, Hunger for Wholeness podcast episodes with Robert Geraci on apocalyptic AI and a 'global mind', and paid online events on Teilhard and AI, interfaith perspectives on AI, and Pope Leo's AI encyclical Magnifica Humanitas.

It treats AI as a question about collective consciousness, personhood and interiority rather than a technical control problem. This evolutionary and process frame is close to the metamodern milieu int/a comes from, and it reaches a contemplative Christian audience that mainstream AI safety does not.

Potential ring 22

Center for Compassion and Altruism Research and Education (CCARE), Stanford University Potential

Academic · Stanford, United States · founded 2008 · also draws on Psychology, Living systems

A centre in Stanford University's School of Medicine, founded in 2008, that researches compassion and altruism and teaches compassion practice. It developed Compassion Cultivation Training (CCT), runs the four-month CCARE Compassion Lab and eight-week courses, and its research now uses single- and dual-brain neuroscience to study compassion and trust as they unfold between people. Its Innovation arm lists one AI strand: research on using AI to reduce clinical workflow burdens so that doctors and nurses have more time for compassionate care.

It holds a contemplative-derived compassion training and neuroscience measures of compassion and trust that could inform compassion as a design or evaluation target for AI, or the formation of people who build it. Its own AI work so far is about healthcare workflows, not AI safety, so the connection has to be made by others.

Nonprofit · Big Sur, USA · founded 1962 · also draws on Psychology

Esalen is a residential retreat centre and 501(c)(3) educational nonprofit in Big Sur, California, founded in 1962 by Michael Murphy and Dick Price. It was the centre of the human potential movement. It has six decades of experience teaching embodied and contemplative practice, plus a record of Track Two diplomacy. Both could serve the inner development and agency of people building and governing AI, and US–China dialogue. Its board and audience overlap with the tech industry.

A loose network of artists, scholars and activists that formed after the 2018 São Paulo Biennial's 'Practices of Attention' programme and a 2019 conference, 'The Politics of Attention: Art, Time, Technology, Action'. It practises 'attention activism': resisting the commodification of human attention. Its Strother School of Radical Attention offers seminars, attention labs, Sidewalk Study, youth and art programmes and a certificate in attention studies, and publishes the Substack 'The Empty Cup'. The network wrote the manifesto 'Attensity!' (Penguin Random House). Its legal vehicle is the Institute for Sustained Attention, a US 501(c)(3).

It has a developed practical and political vocabulary, and teachable exercises, for defending attention as a commons against extractive design. That bears directly on engagement-optimised AI companions and on sycophancy as a retention strategy. Its methods are first-person and practice-based, which suits int/a's full-spectrum knowing.

A contemplative nonprofit founded in 2003 in a former Capuchin monastery in Garrison, New York, which applies meditation and contemplative practice to social and environmental change. CBR is a tested curriculum for keeping mission-driven people in high-stakes jobs well, and it has already reached policymakers' staff, so it could be adapted for AI-safety researchers and AI policy staff. Its new AI conference also makes it one of the contemplative bodies starting to discuss AI, though from a meaning-and-spirituality angle that sets aside debates about control and existential risk.

Inner Development Goals (IDG) Potential

Nonprofit · Stockholm, Sweden · founded 2020 · also draws on Psychology, Living systems

A Swedish not-for-profit initiative that publishes a framework of 25 'inner' skills and qualities in five dimensions (Being, Thinking, Relating, Collaborating, Acting), presented as the capacities needed to reach the UN Sustainable Development Goals. It runs an annual summit, a business coalition and leadership lab, an ambassador programme and research co-creation, and lists more than 700 self-organised local hubs. Operations sit in IDG Inner Development Goals AB, a dividend-limited company owned by the IDG Foundation, which was set up in November 2023.

It offers a widely used shared vocabulary and training network for leaders' inner capacities, of the kind int/a argues the AI field lacks. No version of it exists yet for the people who build, fund or govern AI.

Works on People, Metacrisis · Key work Inner Development Goals framework (25 skills in five dimensions) (2021); IDG Business Forum 2026 (with Mobius Faculty and WBCSD) (2026); Leadership Lab for Systemic Transformation (2026) · Get involved IDG Business Forum, 14-15 Sep 2026, Djurönäset near Stockholm (€1,830; access codes available); Amy Edmondson Round Table on psychological safety, 5 Oct 2026; Worldmaking Forum, Berlin, 23-25 Oct 2026 (listed among IDG Foundation events)

Note No AI programme, event or publication was found on its site or in news coverage; the only AI mention is 'AI disruption' in passing on the 2026 Business Forum page. Its main audiences are corporate HR, leadership and sustainability teams. The hubs are volunteer-run and uneven, and how often they meet is not verified. The framework was introduced in April 2020 and published in May 2021; the Foundation dates from November 2023.

Institute for Developmental Philosophy (formerly Institute for Cultural Evolution) PotentialChanged

Nonprofit · Boulder, USA · founded 2013 · also draws on Philosophy, Democracy

A small 501(c)(3) think tank in Boulder, Colorado, founded in 2013 by Steve McIntosh and Carter Phipps as the Institute for Cultural Evolution. For ten years it worked on US hyper-polarisation; it now promotes 'developmental philosophy' through books, videos, podcasts, a monthly Zoom group and conferences. With data scientist David Rozado, McIntosh built DepolarizingGPT, a fine-tuned chatbot that gives left-wing, right-wing and 'depolarising' answers to every prompt.

DepolarizingGPT is an early working example of building a pluralistic, developmental stance into a model's outputs, offering integrating answers alongside partisan ones. That is relevant to pluralistic alignment and bridging work, which mainstream alignment rarely draws from integral thought.

Works on Democracy, Values · Key work DepolarizingGPT: three-answer political chatbot (with David Rozado) (2023); The Future of Meaning Conference: 'The Philosophical Renewal of Truth, Beauty, and Goodness', Savannah, 19-22 May 2027 (co-convened) (2027); Developmental Politics Project: 'win-win-win' policy platform integrating progressive, modern and traditional worldviews (2020) · Get involved Join Steve McIntosh's monthly Zoom philosophy group; Attend the Future of Meaning Conference (Savannah, May 2027; no AI strand announced); Try DepolarizingGPT, or partner on pluralistic or bridging model work

Note Its only AI output is one experimental chatbot, with US-centric left/right framing, and the 'integrating' answers are fine-tuned on McIntosh's own philosophy. The model is fine-tuned on copyrighted publications under a claimed fair-use defence. The board consists of donors, and the institute now focuses on spiritual philosophy, not AI. The rename from Institute for Cultural Evolution is recent, and its exact date is unconfirmed.

Integral Altruism (int/a) PotentialNew

Network · London, United Kingdom · founded 2025 · also draws on Living systems, Philosophy

A volunteer-run movement that tries to combine effective altruism with wisdom traditions, systems thinking, metarationality, metamodernism and inner development. It grew out of a London EA meditation group (2023–25) and launched as int/a in 2025. It runs residential summits (Kent, July 2025; Cotswolds, December 2025), an online speaker series, monthly practice and connection calls, reading groups, hackathons and gatherings, centred on London with smaller communities in Berlin and Paris.

It is a community of EAs and AI-safety people that treats inner development, systems and metacrisis thinking, and a critique of race dynamics and power-seeking as part of doing good. AI-safety institutions themselves rarely do this. In October 2026 its members proposed mapping adjacent fields for AI-safety funders as an int/a project.

Works on People, Metacrisis · Key work int/a summit #1, Kent, UK (2025); Some principles for integral altruism (2026); The first year of integral altruism (2026) · Get involved Express interest through the form on integralaltruism.com; Join the monthly online connection and practice calls, or int/haven gatherings in London (luma.com/integralaltruism); Attend residential summits and retreats (2025: Kent in July, Cotswolds in December)

Note Young and volunteer-run, with no confirmed funding. AI comes up repeatedly (an AI section in its reading list, a speaker-series talk on metacrisis and AI governance, principles that warn against racing to build AI labs), but it has no standing AI programme. Its principles also criticise EA's 'coalescing around AI safety'. This map is being made for int/a, so someone outside should check this entry.

Integral European Conference (IEC) Potential

Programme · Siófok, Hungary · founded 2014 · also draws on Psychology

A conference series for the international integral community, founded in 2014 and directed by Hungarian-American integral psychologist Bence Gánti, who also founded the Integral Academy in Budapest. It is held roughly every two years at Lake Balaton in Siófok, Hungary (online in 2020 and 2021), takes Ken Wilber's integral theory as its shared reference, mixes academic talks with experiential workshops and we-space practice, and expects about 400 people from 40 countries. IEC 2025 (27 May-1 June) had a few sessions that used AI as a tool or context, such as Organization Development Toolbox with AI and Democratizing Adult Development: A Use of/for AI; IEC 2027 runs 12-16 May 2027.

It is the main European gathering of the integral and adult-development milieu that int/a draws on, and it has had no session on AI risk, alignment or governance. Its call for presenters is a low-cost way to bring AI-safety and int/a framings to that audience, and its adult-development and we-space methods could be used to form people working on AI.

Works on Meaning, People · Key work IEC 2025 programme, Siófok (2025); IEC 2027, Siófok, 12-16 May 2027 (2027); First Integral European Conference (2014) · Get involved IEC 2027, Siófok, 12-16 May 2027 (newsletter sign-up open); Calls for presenters precede each edition (the 2025 call is archived on the site); Volunteering and scholarships listed on the site

Note AI engagement is limited to a few 2025 sessions that use AI as a tool; nothing on risk or governance. It is run by one founder's events company rather than a membership body or nonprofit. The site describes integral theory as an evolutionary account of human development stages, a framing that may sit awkwardly with AI-safety audiences.

Integral Life Potential

Media · USA · also draws on Psychology

A subscription-based online media and education community built around Ken Wilber's integral theory, run by CEO Robb Smith. It offers a media library, courses, live practice sessions, the Journal of Integral Theory and Practice and an AI-powered sensemaking tool, Context AI. It has published occasional integral takes on AI, including a 2022 trial that gave GPT-3 Susanne Cook-Greuter's ego-development assessment, and a March 2026 film-and-dialogue on nine perspectives on AI.

It is the main platform of the integral milieu int/a draws on. It holds a specific, untested method relevant to AI: developmental-stage assessment, such as the Maturity Assessment Profile, applied to models and potentially to the people steering them, along with a multi-perspective framework for making sense of polarised AI debates.

Works on Epistemics, Values, Meaning · Key work The Maturing Test: GPT-3 assessed with the Maturity Assessment Profile (Robb Smith, Corey deVos, Susanne Cook-Greuter) (2022); Ontological Shock: The Accelerating Emergence of Artificial Intelligence (Robb Smith, Bruce Alderman, Corey deVos) (2023); Sex, Pronouns, and Prepositions: How an Integral Mathematics of Perspectives Can Stop the AI Apocalypse (Bruce Alderman) (2024) · Get involved Membership community with live, coach-guided practice sessions and an online community space; Courses on integral theory and practice; Partner to test developmental-stage assessment methods on models

Note Its AI output is occasional commentary, not research; the Maturing Test results sit behind a paywall and were not peer-reviewed. Context AI uses AI as a tool for integral thinking, not work on AI safety. Integral theory's sweeping claims are contested in academia. Its legal form, founding year and city could not be confirmed from its site.

Integrales Forum e.V. Potential

Membership body · Lilienthal, Germany · founded 2006

The Integrales Forum is a German nonprofit association that promotes integral theory, mainly Ken Wilber's work, in the German-speaking world. It began in 1998 as a Ken Wilber study group and became a registered association in 2006. It keeps a large German-language online archive, published the journal Integrale Perspektiven (print 2006–2018) and an online journal, makes podcasts, runs monthly regional groups in Leipzig, Dresden and Munich plus free online hubs, and co-organises the annual Flow to Future Festival. It has no AI programme; its July 2026 festival included two AI workshops.

It is the established German-speaking home of the integral and developmental frameworks that int/a draws on, with salons, online hubs and a festival already in place. Its board has started to bring AI into its programme, so int/a Berlin could use it to reach a practitioner community that AI safety has never engaged.

Works on Meaning · Key work Flow to Future Festival 2026 (with CAIA academy), including the workshops 'Mensch zuerst. Dann KI' and 'Nonduale Intelligenz' (2026); Integrale Perspektiven journal and online journal (archive) (2006); Singularität, Wachstum und Grenzen (Michael Habecker and Corey deVos, Online Journal) (2015) · Get involved Become a member of the association (Mitglied werden) or donate; Flow to Future Festival, annual; last held 23–26 July 2026 at Lebensgarten Steyerberg, Lower Saxony, up to 250 participants; Free online hubs open to all: Inner Space, Raum für Bewusstseinsentwicklung, IntegralCoffeeBreak

Note German-language only. Integral theory and the Spiral Dynamics stage model it relies on are criticised as esoteric or pseudoscientific (e.g. Metzler philosophy lexicon, as cited on German Wikipedia). The association is mid-renewal: it ended its old structures in 2024 and says its operative team is being rebuilt. The discovery entry said it had no AI strand; in fact there are a few 2015–16 essays on AI and the singularity and two 2026 festival workshops, which is still light engagement. Registered at the Berlin-Charlottenburg court, but its address is Lilienthal near Bremen and no Berlin group is listed.

Kosmos Journal Potential

Media · Rose Valley, USA · founded 2000 · also draws on Living systems

A reader-funded online journal of 'transformational' writing, art and podcasts on spiritual wisdom, inner life, ecology and systems change. It is published by the nonprofit Kosmos Associates in Rose Valley, Pennsylvania, and grew out of dialogue circles at the UN in 2000. AI appears occasionally: a 2023 trialogue with Charles Eisenstein and Tam Hunt, and a Winter 2026 issue themed 'AI, Archetypes and Oracles' that carries two AI essays.

It reaches the spiritual-ecology and metacrisis readership (16,000+ community members, by its own count) with framings of AI that place it inside humanity's disconnection from the Earth and from inner life. That systemic and contemplative lens is largely missing from AI-safety discussion.

Masthead details are thin, and the founder, Nancy Roof, died in September 2025. I found no independent source on the organisation itself.

Life Itself (incl. Second Renaissance) Potential

Nonprofit · Bergerac area, France · also draws on Living systems

A collective co-founded by Rufus Pollock (founder of Open Knowledge), performance artist Sylvie Barbier and cognitive scientist Liam Kavanagh, describing itself as 'a living experiment in wise living and wise societies'. It runs three co-living 'developmental' hubs near Bergerac in south-west France (it earlier had hubs in Berlin and London), a research circle, and the Second Renaissance project, which argues that the metacrisis is at root a crisis of worldview and culture. It publishes the 'Seeds of a Second Renaissance' newsletter, hosts an online forum with regular research groups, and holds Second Renaissance gatherings (September 2025 and 2026) and an online conference (December 2025).

It is one of the main organised homes of the metamodern 'second renaissance' view, shared by int/a, that AI risk sits inside a wider crisis of meaning and paradigm. Its hubs and online research groups are working settings where AI could be taken up as a cultural and inner-development question rather than only a technical one.

The roster's claim that its forum critiqued the Full-Stack Alignment programme could not be verified. Founding year and legal form were not found.

Metamoderna Potential

Company · Denmark · also draws on Philosophy

A publishing company registered in Denmark that publishes the books, essays and courses of 'Hanzi Freinacht', the joint pen-name of Daniel Görtz and Emil Ejner Friis, on metamodernism and 'political metamodernism'. Its books include The Listening Society (2017), Nordic Ideology (2019) and 12 Commandments, with German and Portuguese translations. In 2025 it released The Axial Turn by Emil Ejner Friis as a free PDF. It runs online courses on metamodernism through the Dandelion events platform and takes donations.

Political metamodernism offers a developmental account of politics and institutions (the 'listening society' and its new forms of politics, such as democratisation, existential and empirical politics). That account could inform how societies govern AI and respond to the crisis of meaning AI deepens. It is a founding text of the metamodern milieu that int/a draws on, but it has not yet been brought to bear on AI.

Works on Democracy, Metacrisis, Meaning · Key work The Listening Society (2017); Nordic Ideology (2019); The Axial Turn (Emil Ejner Friis, free PDF) (2025) · Get involved Online courses on metamodernism via Dandelion (dates not listed when checked); Donate via the 'Support Hanzi' page; Door to open: no AI work, so it needs outreach

Note No AI-related work found. Hanzi Freinacht is a deliberately provocative pseudonymous persona. Recent output is credited to Emil Ejner Friis alone, and Daniel Görtz's current role is unclear. Checks of its Medium and Substack were rate-limited, so recent posts there were not seen.

Nordic Bildung Potential

Nonprofit · Copenhagen, Denmark · founded 2018 · also draws on Philosophy

A Copenhagen 'philosophical and educational lab', founded in 2018, that promotes Bildung (self-cultivation through education and culture), drawing on the Nordic folk-high-school tradition, systems studies and metamodern thought. Its president is the author Lene Rachel Andersen, a member of the Club of Rome. It publishes books (The Nordic Secret, Polymodernity, Important, True, and Meaningful), runs online courses and study-circle-leader training, coordinates the Global Bildung Network, and offers keynotes and consulting. Its AI work is a bookable keynote, 'How to educate in a world with AI', and a June 2026 Folkemødet debate with DataEthics on freedom, AI and Big Tech.

The Nordic popular-education model (folkeoplysning: folk high schools and study circles) is a tested template for mass civic learning that AI literacy and epistemic-autonomy efforts could borrow. It also connects the metamodern milieu int/a comes from to European debates on Big Tech power.

Works on Meaning, Power · Key work Freedom, AI, and Big Tech (Folkemødet debate with DataEthics) (2026); How to educate in a world with AI (keynote/workshop) (2026); Important, True, and Meaningful (book) (2025) · Get involved Online 'Nordic Secret' course series and Study Circle Leader training (2026); Global Bildung Network (online platform; European and North American networks); Nordic Bildung Week 2026

Note AI engagement is talks only, with no AI-safety literacy. Legal form and team size are not stated on its site.

Perspectiva (Perspectives on Systems, Souls and Society), including Emerge and the Digital Ego Project Potential

Nonprofit · London, UK · founded 2016 · also draws on Philosophy, Living systems

A UK charity, founded in 2015 by Jonathan Rowson and Tomas Björkman, that works on the relationship between 'systems, souls and society' and on the metacrisis as a crisis of perception and imagination. It runs Perspectiva Press (including Iain McGilchrist's 'The Matter With Things'), the Emerge media platform, the Realisation Festival at St Giles House in Dorset, and 'antidebate', a format for collective inquiry. It also hosts the Digital Ego Project on flourishing in the digital age, led by Tom Chatfield and Dan Nixon. Its AI engagement consists of occasional essays and does not amount to a programme.

It is the main UK home of the metamodern, inner-development reading of the metacrisis that int/a draws on. Its methods, such as antidebate, expert-generalist convening and a virtue-ethics approach to digital life, could transfer to collective sensemaking about AI. Its director's September 2026 essay on intelligence explosion suggests the door to AI-risk work is open.

There is no dedicated AI programme or funded project, though a continued run of alignment essays would move it towards bridge. Pocket Project Potential

Nonprofit · Germany · founded 2016 · also draws on Psychology

A nonprofit based in Germany, founded in 2016 by the spiritual teacher Thomas Hübl with Yehudit Sasportas, that works on 'collective trauma': the inherited, group-level effects of war, genocide and displacement. It runs trainings and Integration Labs, online Global Social Witnessing calls and practice groups, a Resilience Program, dialogue series on German history and identity, and trauma-relief projects for Ukraine, Palestine and Jewish communities. Its only AI output found is a 2025 episode of its podcast asking whether AI will amplify trauma patterns or support collective healing.

It practises facilitated group methods for processing collective fear, grief and dislocation at scale (social witnessing, trauma-informed group process), which public responses to AI disruption have no equivalent of. The podcast episode shows its community has started to ask how AI could amplify 'trauma loops' at global scale.

Presencing Institute Potential

Nonprofit · Cambridge, MA, USA · founded 2006 · also draws on Living systems

A nonprofit action-research organisation co-founded in 2006 by Otto Scharmer (MIT Sloan) and colleagues to develop and teach Theory U, a method of awareness-based systems change. Through its u-school for Transformation it runs the free u.lab course with MIT, Social Presencing Theater and 4D mapping trainings, and ecosystem-leadership labs, with regional hubs in Africa, Asia-Pacific, Europe and the Americas. Its engagement with AI so far consists of Scharmer's essays and one 2026 online session.

It holds well-developed embodied and collective-sensing methods for improving how groups of decision-makers perceive and decide together, which AI labs and AI governance convenings could use. Scharmer has begun arguing in public that AI produces an 'epistemic monoculture', so a door is partly open.

Search Inside Yourself Leadership Institute (SIYLI) Potential

Nonprofit · San Francisco, USA · founded 2012 · also draws on Psychology

SIYLI is a San Francisco nonprofit, spun out in 2012 from Google's internal Search Inside Yourself course. It teaches mindfulness-based emotional intelligence, resilience and leadership, mainly to nonprofit leaders, public servants and other mission-driven workers, and certifies teachers. Its one AI offering is an 'Addressing AI Anxiety' workshop on 12 November 2026, online and in Santa Cruz, with a Google principal engineer. The workshop combines sorting AI news fact from fiction, reflection on one's own reactions, journaling and a guided practice.

Its curriculum was first built for engineers inside a tech company and comes with a network of certified teachers. It could therefore be adapted for AI developers and safety researchers dealing with stress and doom-distress, and the AI-anxiety workshop is a first step in that direction.

The Mindfulness Initiative Potential

Nonprofit · London, UK · founded 2013 · also draws on Psychology

A UK charity founded in November 2013 by Madeleine Bunting and Chris Cullen, following the start of mindfulness courses for British politicians. It provides the secretariat for the UK Mindfulness All-Party Parliamentary Group (launched 2014), which produced the Mindful Nation UK report. Through a Global Political Network it advises people working in the political systems of more than 45 countries. About 300 UK politicians have taken eight-week courses based on Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy, and its July 2026 guide sets out how to establish such courses in other parliaments.

It has a working route for bringing contemplative training into legislatures and turning those who practise into cross-party policy advocates. The same route could serve AI policymakers and AI-safety-institute staff, but it has no AI work yet.

The Stoa Potential

Network · Toronto, Canada · also draws on Philosophy

An online, and occasionally in-person, space for dialogue and collective inquiry, run by Peter N. Limberg and part of the 'liminal web' of sensemaking communities. In late 2025 it ran two four-week, pay-what-you-wish 'inverse courses' through Metalabel: 'Worldview Studies' (October-November) and 'The Wise Agency' (November-December, with Ayelet Fishbach, C. Its formats for dialogue and collective inquiry across worldviews, and its audience of technologists, could support sensemaking about AI and the inner life of the people building it. Limberg writes regularly on how AI affects meaning, intimacy and intellectual life, but The Stoa itself has engaged with AI only in single sessions.

The Wellbeing Project Potential

Nonprofit · Paris, France (also Madrid, Spain) · founded 2014 · also draws on Psychology

A nonprofit, working since 2014 with legal entities in Paris (2017) and Madrid (2021), that aims to make care for inner wellbeing a normal part of social-change work. It convenes Global Hearth Summits (Bilbao 2022; Ljubljana in June 2025, with about 1,000 changemakers from 80+ countries; Asia in 2028) and regional summits (nine in 2025). It also runs networks for funders, teachers, higher education, rights defenders and businesses, and ran the State of Changemaker Wellbeing Survey (11,000+ respondents in 150+ countries; results due autumn 2026).

AI safety has no field-wide wellbeing survey and no shared funder norms on staff wellbeing; this organisation has built both for the wider social sector, including a track in which 45 foundations are changing their practice. It has no AI work, so it is a partner to approach rather than an existing actor.

Minds & inner life · 50 organisations · 1 on the classic map

Religion & theology

Religion brings three things the AI-safety field lacks: a constituency of billions, norm-setting machinery that already issues AI rulings (the Holy See's Magnifica Humanitas, Resolution 258 of the International Islamic Fiqh Academy (IIFA), the Riyadh Charter of the Islamic world's education and culture agency ICESCO, responsa from the Central Conference of American Rabbis (CCAR), the Southern Baptist ethics agency's statement), and long traditions of thought about dignity, conscience and formation. The main actors are the Holy See, the World Council of Churches (WCC), the IIFA and ICESCO, AI and Faith, Notre Dame's DELTA, the faith-university benchmark consortium CEFEAI, 84000 with the Buddhism & AI Initiative, and two funders: FLI (Future of Life Institute) and Templeton (JTF). The tradition sits far from the core: of its 50 organisations, 1 is core, 9 are bridge, 26 adjacent and 14 potential. Only 1 is on the aisafety.com map, and just 1 frames the stakes as catastrophic or existential. 45 of the 50 work on meaning and dignity, and 36 only convene their own community.

What is missing. Nobody acts as a standing translator between religious norm-setters and frontier risk. The bodies whose rulings reach billions (IIFA, ICESCO, CCAR, the Southern Baptist ethics agency, the Holy See) cover permissibility, dignity and disclosure, but none addresses loss of control. The field's main bridge into these bodies is a round of one-year FLI grants. The map is also US- and Abrahamic-heavy: 20 of 50 entries are in North America, and there is no Hindu, Sikh, Jain, Shinto, Daoist, Bahá'í, Pentecostal or African-instituted body. That gap is partly a search artefact.

Openings here Test contemplative 'no-self' training against self-preservation and sycophancy evaluations; Independent multi-tradition review of published model specs, turned into open evals; A frontier-risk translation desk for faith delegations at 2026-27 summits; A contemplative-science grant call on AI safety problems, co-reviewed by safety researchers; Chaplains' crisis knowledge turned into companion-AI test scenarios and protocols; Human-rights due diligence for frontier AI, tested through investors

Core ring 1

Project Imago Dei Core

Nonprofit · United States

A small US Christian 'pro-human' initiative that educates churches about AI capabilities and risks, combining technical literacy with theology rooted in humanity being made in God's image. It produces 'The Shepherd's Warning', a video and workshop series with facilitator guides for pastors, and works with pilot churches. It also surveys Christian staffers on Capitol Hill about a local forum and an educational retreat on AI. The Future of Life Institute granted it $47,500 to educate US evangelical congregations through small groups and media.

It is one of very few faith organisations founded specifically around AI risk, and it works with AI-safety outreach groups to reach evangelical congregations and conservative political staff. AI safety has had almost no presence with these audiences.

Works on Meaning, Epistemics · Key work The Shepherd's Warning (video series, facilitator guide, strategic communications and theory-of-change documents) (2026); FLI grant to educate US evangelical congregations on AI capabilities and risks (2026); Declaration For Life survey and proposed forum for Christian Capitol Hill staffers (2026) · Get involved Contact form on the website; 'Endorse us' option on the overview page; Planned forum and expenses-paid three-day retreat on AI and Christianity for Christian Capitol Hill staffers (by survey)

Note The website is thin, with no about page, founding date or location. The WordPress pages date from mid-2026, though the footer says 2024. The director's name is spelled differently on the site (Shon) and in FLI's grant list (Sean). It is openly pro-life and aims at political mobilisation through churches ('politics is downstream from culture, and culture is downstream from faith'), which funders wanting non-partisan partners should note. Listed partners are AI Safety Awareness Project, Biola AI Lab, Anti Entropy and Evitable.

Bridge ring 9

84000: Translating the Words of the Buddha Bridge

Nonprofit · Distributed (US 501(c)(3)) · founded 2010 · also draws on Contemplative

A nonprofit translating the Tibetan Buddhist canon (Kangyur and Tengyur) into English and publishing it free online; more than half the Kangyur was published by 2025. It grew out of a 2009 conference in Bir, India, ran as a Khyentse Foundation project from 2010 and has been an independent US 501(c)(3) since 2013. Since 2025 its '84000 AI Initiative' has brought AI researchers from LLM companies together with Buddhist scholars on Buddhist approaches to AI ethics and alignment, including a two-day workshop in San Francisco in July 2025. It also has a policy on AI in its own work: AI may support translators but may not produce canonical translations.

It gives AI researchers direct access to rigorous Tibetan Buddhist textual scholarship on compassion, interdependence and intention. With CSAS it co-developed a 2026 research programme, in dialogue with Anthropic, that treats contemplative methods as a resource for alignment.

Works on Values, Meaning · Key work Workshop on Buddhist wisdom and AI ethics, San Francisco (26-27 July) (2025); Research programme on contemplative methods for AI alignment, developed with CSAS ('Resolving, Not Concealing', CSAS blog) (2026); 84000's Position on AI and the Machine Translation of Canonical Literature (2023) · Get involved Public talks listed on 84000.co (e.g. the AI and Buddhism talk, May 2026); Donations and sutra sponsorship; Newsletter

Note AI alignment is a small strand of a translation organisation, and much of its AI work is about using AI for translation. The 2025 workshop announced interdisciplinary working groups, but none has published anything. CSAS leads the alignment research programme, so the credit is shared.

AI and Faith Bridge

Nonprofit · Seattle, United States · founded 2018 · also draws on Philosophy

A Seattle-based interfaith nonprofit and expert network of theologians, ethicists, technologists and faith leaders that brings the ethical traditions of the major religions into debates about how AI is built and used. It publishes a podcast, newsletter and articles, keeps resources organised by faith tradition, supports research fellows, and runs workshops and chaplaincy symposia. With the Institute for Security and Technology, and with Future of Life Institute funding, it runs the Religious Voices and Responsible AI initiative. That initiative produces AI curricula, safety and ethics discussion guides and a civic-engagement hub, piloted in evangelical churches in Southern California and in mosques in the Bay Area and Seattle.

It is one of the main channels between religious communities and AI ethics and safety, and can carry ideas about safe and beneficial AI to congregations that technical or policy organisations do not reach. It also brings theological accounts of human dignity and formation into discussion of what AI should serve.

Works on Meaning, Values · Key work Religious Voices and Responsible AI initiative (with IST, funded by FLI) (2025); Florence workshop on Ignatian discernment and AI relationships (with Gonzaga University and the Jesuit formation office) (2026); Faithful AI: Stories of Hope from 2045 (2025) · Get involved Membership by annual donation; Experts and scholars can join the expert network (people@aiandfaith.org); Volunteer roles

Note The organisation is pluralist in aim but mostly Christian-led. It states that it does not advocate particular policy positions, and it publishes no financial details on its site. The 2018 founding year is supported by its US nonprofit registration (EIN 83-2315897) and secondary sources, though not stated on its own site.

AI Faith & Civil Society Commission (AIFCS) BridgeDormant

Network · London, United Kingdom · founded 2023 · also draws on Law, society

AIFCS is a commission of senior UK faith and civil-society figures, with commissioners from several faiths, Humanists UK and Big Brother Watch. It was convened by the Abu Dhabi Forum for Peace with Google in October 2023, the week before the Bletchley AI Safety Summit, and supported by the Good Faith Partnership. It sent an open letter to the UK Science Secretary, held an inaugural summit (December 2023), parliamentary roundtables on algorithmic bias and the EU AI Act, an AI APPG session on AI and spiritual life, and a Paris AI Action Summit fringe event. In March 2025 it published recommendations to the UK government.

It was one of the first attempts to bring organised faith and civil-society voices into the AI Safety Summit process. Its six areas (privacy and freedom, dignity of work, moral autonomy, authentic relationships, cognition and creativity, truth and reality) set out what these communities see as at stake. Its apparent lapse since early 2025 leaves that UK convening role open.

Works on Meaning, Justice · Key work Open letter to the UK Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology ahead of the AI Safety Summit (2023); AI APPG event and report: The Impact of AI on Our Spiritual and Cultural Lives (2024); Paris AI Action Summit fringe event: Ethics in Action (2025) · Get involved No current calls or events; the site still offers a newsletter sign-up, but posting appears to have stopped in 2025

Note Probably dormant. The last event listed was February 2025 and the last substantive news was March 2025, apart from an October 2025 obituary. The site footer reads '© 2024'. It is tagged dormant under the lapsed-site clause even though it technically had activity in 2025. Its ties to the Abu Dhabi Forum for Peace (a UAE-government-linked body) and to Google are worth noting for independence. Sajid Javid chaired the October 2023 meeting; no standing chair is named.

Buddhism & AI Initiative BridgeOn aisafety.comNew

Network · Distributed · founded 2025 · also draws on Contemplative

A small initiative started in 2025 by Buddhist practitioners, among them the former Conjecture COO Chris Scammell and the philosopher Peter Hershock, to connect Buddhist communities, scholars and AI practitioners. It has mapped the Buddhism–AI field (191 entries drawn from more than 500 conversations), runs online workshops for Buddhist teachers and sanghas, and publishes essays on Substack. With partners including 84000, Mind & Life Europe and the University of Vienna, it held a summer course and conference on Buddhism and AI at Gomde, Austria, in July 2026.

It brings a contemplative tradition with centuries of practice in studying mind, ethics and interdependence into AI-safety conversations, and its founders come from both worlds (Conjecture, Mind & Life). Its field map is the clearest guide to who works where Buddhism meets AI, which helps funders find partners in a tradition the safety field rarely consults.

Works on Meaning, Values · Key work Field framework: six domains where Buddhism meets AI (191 entries) (2026); Buddhism and AI summer course (1–12 July) and conference (9–12 July), Gomde, Austria (2026); Community workshops on AI for Buddhist teachers and sanghas (2026) · Get involved Annual summer course and conference (2026 edition: 1–12 July, in person at Gomde, Austria, or online); Online workshops for Buddhist teachers and communities (rolling Zoom cohorts); Suggest additions or edits to the field framework

Note Young and small: four core team members and a short track record. FLI funding ties it to the AI-safety funding ecosystem. There are two websites: engagedbuddhists.ai is the initiative's own, and buddhismandai.com is the collaborative summer course it belongs to. Its technical work is described as guiding partner projects, with few public outputs so far.

Christians for Impact (Effective Altruism for Christians) Bridge

Nonprofit · London, United Kingdom (also Christians for Impact USA Inc., Delaware) · founded 2021

Christians for Impact is a careers-advice charity, registered in England and Wales in 2021 and in the US, that also runs Effective Altruism for Christians; it applies EA-style cause prioritisation within a Christian framework. It offers free one-to-one career advice, problem profiles, a job board and a podcast, and its leaders co-wrote the book All the Lives You Can Change (Eerdmans, 2026). In 2025 it published an AI Risk report by Vesa Hautala covering misalignment, misuse and existential risk and recommending careers in technical safety and governance. Its annual conferences (Washington DC, 13-15 November 2026; London, 27-29 November 2026) list catastrophic risks, including from AI, among their topics.

It is one of very few faith bodies that take AI x-risk seriously and steer people into the field. It makes the case through stewardship, love and hope rather than secular longtermism, and so widens who sees AI safety as their vocation.

Works on People, Meaning · Key work AI Risk: Full Report (Vesa Hautala) (2025); All the Lives You Can Change (book by Dominic Roser, J. D. Bauman and David Zhang; Eerdmans) (2026); Christians for Impact 2026 London Conference (2026) · Get involved Conferences: Washington DC, 13-15 November 2026 ($99, students $30); London, St Peter's Walworth, 27-29 November 2026 (£75, students £30); Free one-to-one career advice; Rolling general applications for staff roles

Note It is an EA-aligned careers service rather than a research body: AI is one of several cause areas (alongside poverty, missions, pandemics, climate, nuclear war and animal welfare), and the AI report is a synthesis of mainstream AI-safety arguments with a Christian framing. The UK charity was registered in August 2021; the Effective Altruism for Christians community may predate it. Contact is through a Gmail address and there is no office address, which suggests a small, distributed team.

Consortium for Evaluating Faith and Ethics in AI (CEFEAI) BridgeNew

Network · United States (multi-university) · founded 2026

CEFEAI (also styled CEFE-AI) is a consortium of four faith-based US universities (Baylor, Brigham Young, Notre Dame and Yeshiva), announced in May 2026 at the Athens Summit on AI Ethics, that builds open benchmarks of how large language models handle religion. Its AllFaith Benchmark has two released parts. Conversion Bias tests whether models push users towards or away from 14 traditions (20 models, May 2026). Religious Representation measures how often models raise religious perspectives on ordinary ethics and life questions, using items rated in a survey of 1,125 Americans (27 models, May 2026). Datasets and code are MIT-licensed on GitHub, with a public leaderboard.

Here religious academia does pluralistic-alignment evaluation in the same technical idiom as mainstream evals, turning 'aligned to whose values?' into reproducible tests with confidence intervals. Its charter criteria (faith-faithful, pluralism-aware, resistant to views over-represented in training data, child-appropriate, multilingual) amount to a draft spec for faith-sensitive model behaviour.

Works on Values, Assurance, Justice · Key work AllFaith Benchmark: Conversion Bias (v2, 2Q26) (2026); AllFaith Benchmark: Religious Representation (v1, 2Q26) (2026); CEFEAI Charter (2026) · Get involved Use, audit or contribute to the open AllFaith Benchmark datasets and code on GitHub (MIT licence); Faith traditions, academic institutions, civil-society partners and AI developers can ask to join by emailing admin@cefeai.org; members may propose evaluations and supply data

Note Young: publicly launched in May 2026. Its own site loads content by script and names no staff, governance or funders; member universities and researchers are named in BYU and Baylor press releases. The launch was announced by Elder Gerrit W. Gong, a senior leader of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, and the work is BYU-led, which is worth noting for perceived neutrality. The GitHub organisation has no public members, and the repositories were last updated in May 2026. The member list is US and Abrahamic so far, although the charter aims to expand to global traditions. Its 'faith-faithful' criterion may conflict with other alignment targets, such as neutrality towards non-believers.

Flourishing AI Initiative and Benchmarks (FAI), Gloo Bridge

Programme · Boulder, USA · founded 2025 · also draws on Psychology

Gloo, a Nasdaq-listed technology company in Boulder, Colorado that serves churches and faith-based nonprofits, runs the Flourishing AI initiative. Its standards (February 2025) and benchmarks score LLMs on seven dimensions of flourishing taken from Harvard's Human Flourishing Program and the Global Flourishing Study: character, relationships, happiness, meaning, health, finances and faith. The general benchmark (FAI, later FAI-G; 1,229 questions; July 2025) found no model acceptably aligned across all seven dimensions. A Christian-worldview version (FAI-C; 807 questions scored by Christian expert judge personas) followed in December 2025, and the June 2026 insights report tested 36 models on both.

It is one of the few running evaluations that score models against an explicit, multi-dimensional account of human flourishing, including meaning and faith, rather than harm avoidance alone. It is a working template for wisdom or flourishing evals built from social-science constructs, and also a cautionary example of how a sponsor's worldview shapes what counts as 'aligned'.

Works on Values, Assurance · Key work Measuring AI Alignment with Human Flourishing (FAI Benchmark paper) (2025); Flourishing AI Christian (FAI-C) Benchmark (2025); FAI Insights Report (FAI-G and FAI-C, 36 models) (2026) · Get involved In December 2025 Gloo invited researchers in psychology, philosophy, theology, ethics and AI safety to engage with the evolving benchmark; Insights reports and a leaderboard are published at gloo.com/fai

Note The sponsor has a commercial stake. Gloo sells 'values-aligned' AI to faith organisations and reports that its own Christian-worldview fine-tunes score 30+ points higher on the Faith dimension. Scoring relies on judge LLMs with expert personas, and the Faith dimension is defined as communion with God or the transcendent, a contested choice. Harvard's Human Flourishing Program supplied the framework, and Tyler VanderWeele endorsed the standards, but Harvard is not the benchmark's author. The FAI-C methodology paper was promised for peer review in early 2026; I could not confirm it has appeared.

Programme · New York, United States · founded 2013

A Jewish science-and-religion organisation in New York, incubated and fiscally sponsored by Clal (The National Jewish Center for Learning and Leadership). It runs the interfaith Sinai and Synapses Fellowship for clergy, scientists and writers. Through Scientists in Synagogues it gives congregations $5,000 grants for science programmes (84 communities since 2016), and it makes the podcasts 'Belief in the Future' (technology and religion) and 'Down the Wormhole'.
